messages.body_snippet:
Hi,

I got the same error on this test dataset.
The protein you sent me is actually a protein group. The useNumProteinsColumn parameter controls what PD converter does with protein groups. Please try

messages.subject: Re: Error in .mergeAnnotation(input, annotation) : ** Please check the annotation file. The channel name must be matched with that in input data.

input.pd <- MSstatsTMT::PDtoMSstatsTMTFormat(input = raw.pd, annotation = annotation.pd)

messages.body_snippet:
How is your code matching the Abundance column in the PSM report with the annotation file?

On Thursday, 1 July 2021 at 15:08:38 UTC+2 Tobias Kockmann wrote:
> all of these commands give the same erro

messages.subject: Re: Error in .mergeAnnotation(input, annotation) : ** Please check the annotation file. The channel name must be matched with that in input data.
messages.subject_clean: Error in .mergeAnnotation(input, annotation) : ** Please check the annotation file. The channel name must be matched with that in input data.
messages.body_plain:
That shouldn't be a problem - it matched correctly for the protein you sent me when the protein group was not removed. Before, the error was caused by the fact that all the data were filtered out, so unique(input$Channel) was empty, and unique(annotation$Channel) was not. This is why I need to see some more data to see the error not confounded with a different problem

To answer your question, columns are converted: Abundance.130 -> Abundance130, melted to a Channel column Abundance130 -> 130 and then merged with the annotation.

messages.body_plain:
Since you mention the documentation. I am not sure what to make of:

useNumProteinsColumn
logical, TURE(default) remove shared peptides by information of # Proteins column in PSM sheet.

useUniquePeptide
logical, if TRUE (default) removes peptides that are assigned for more than one proteins. We assume to use unique peptide for each protein.

It kind of sounds like both parameters are doing the same thing. Setting useNumProteinsColumn = TRUE will remove all peptides with Number.of.Proteins > 1 ??? How is uniqueness judged? Where is the difference between being unique and being assigned to a signle protein/protein group???

messages.body_plain:
Hi,
this is PD-specific. In most converters, we remove shared peptides simply by counting proteins per peptide (unique = count == 1) - that' what the useUniquePeptide parameter does. In PD, there is additional information in the column with protein counts. This way, user can remove peptides that belong to more than one protein according to PD counts (in this case, these proteins are in a single protein group). This second meaning is not used in any other converter.
Best,
Mateusz

Hi Mateusz,

Will the log file be ok for the session info? I am attaching it, and here are the scripts:

library(MSstats)
library(MSstatsTMT)
library(tidyr)
library(dplyr)
raw.pd <- read.delim("~/../bHPRP/210617_eIF6_MLL-AF9_TMT6_FAIMS_F_with_human_EIF6_PSMs.txt")
colnames(raw.pd)
length(unique(raw.pd$Protein.Accessions))
annot.pd <- read.delim(file="PD_Annotation.txt", header=TRUE)
runs <- unique(raw.pd$Spectrum.File) # MS runs
Run_info <- data.frame(Run = runs) # initialize the run file
Run_info$Mixture <- ""
Run_info$TechRepMixture <- ""
Run_info$Fraction <- ""
write.csv(Run_info, file = "Run_info.csv", row.names = FALSE)
Run_info_filled <- read.delim(file = "Run_info_filled.txt")
head(Run_info_filled)
channels <- c("126", "127", "128", "129", "130", "131")
mixtures <- unique(Run_info_filled$Mixture)
Group_info <- expand.grid(channels, mixtures)
colnames(Group_info) <- c("Channel", "Mixture")
Group_info$Condition <- ""
Group_info$BioReplicate <- ""
write.table(Group_info, file = "Group_info.txt", row.names = FALSE)
Group_info_filled <- read.delim(file = "Group_info_filled.txt")
annotation <- full_join(Run_info_filled, Group_info_filled)
input.pd <- PDtoMSstatsTMTFormat(input = raw.pd, annotation = annotation)
quant.pd.median.nonorm <- proteinSummarization(data = input.pd,
                                        method="Median",
                                        global_norm=FALSE,
                                        reference_norm=FALSE,
                                        remove_norm_channel = FALSE,
                                        remove_empty_channel = TRUE)
save(quant.pd.median.nonorm, file='quant.pd.median.nonorm.rda')
dataProcessPlotsTMT(data.peptide = input.pd, # PSM-level data
                    data.summarization = quant.pd.median.nonorm, # protein-level data
                    type = 'ProfilePlot', # choice of visualization, can be used for specific protein to see effect
                    width = 21,
                    height = 7,
                    which.Protein = 'P56537')
unique(quant.pd.median.nonorm$Condition)
comparison<-matrix(c(-1,1),nrow=1)
colnames(comparison)<- c("M", "RR")
row.names(comparison)<-c("RR-M")

test_median.pd <- groupComparisonTMT(data = quant.pd.median.nonorm,
                                     contrast.matrix = "pairwise",
                              moderated = TRUE, # do moderated t test
                              adj.method = "BH") # multiple comparison adjustment

groupComparisonPlots(data=test_median.pd,
                     type="VolcanoPlot",
                     logBase.pvalue=10,
                     ProteinName=TRUE, # only for small protein number
                     address="")

** For peptides overlapped between fractions of 1_1, use the fraction with maximal average abundance.

Sudip

In addition, the function documentation says: "Summarizing peptide level quantification to protein level quantification" as if the input data for proteinSummarization is already peptide-level data. Best,
Tobi

messages.subject: Re: MSstatsTMT peptideLevelData?
messages.body_plain:
Hi,
feature = peptide + charge,
it's true that input for proteinSummarization is peptide-level data (ion-level to be precise) [for all converters],
it is possible to generate peptide-level comparison by switching ProteinName column to a peptide ID, but it is not recommended - the workflow consists of summarization to protein-level and then statistical inference (and that's how it was evaluated etc)
Best,
Mateusz

messages.subject: Re: MSstatsTMT peptideLevelData?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Tobi,

Just for clarification, MSstatsTMT can perform peptide significant analysis. A simple solution is to use peptide sequence as protein name. See the following example code:

library(MSstatsTMT)
head(raw.pd)
head(annotation.pd)
input.pd <- PDtoMSstatsTMTFormat(raw.pd, annotation.pd)
head(input.pd)

input.pd$ProteinName <- paste(input.pd$ProteinName, input.pd$PeptideSequence, sep="_")

# peptide-level summary
quant.pd.peptide.msstats <- proteinSummarization(input.pd,
                                         method="msstats",
                                         global_norm=TRUE,
                                         reference_norm=TRUE)

# peptide-level group comparison
test.peptide.pairwise <- groupComparisonTMT(quant.pd.peptide.msstats, moderated = TRUE)

The concern here is that peptide-level estimates are not as reliable as protein-level estimates since peptides have fewer PSMs than proteins.

Best,
Ting

messages.subject: Re: Getting Started with MSstatsPTM
messages.body_plain:
Hi Mi,

Hopefully I can clear up a couple of your questions! In terms of going from PD to MSstatsPTM, we do not have a direct converter right now. I have included a brief piece of code that uses the MSstatsTMT converter to put the raw data into MSstatsPTM format. If you have an example phospho PD dataset you can share, I would be happy to work on building a converter directly into MSstatsPTM.

1. The "PTM" and "Protein" datasets should really be two separate MS runs, one phosphorylated and the other not. The non-phosphorylated run is used to adjusted the modified peptides for changes in protein abundance. If you do not have a unmodified MS run, the package can still be run with the "PTM" data only, you just will not be able to do a protein level adjustment..

2. MSstatsPTM is the correct package and can handle TMT experiments now.

3. The versioning is a little different due to Bioconductor's latest release. All packages in Bioconductor v3.12 (the newest version) require R v4.1. I would recommend upgrading your R to version v4.1 and then upgrading the MSstats packages. You should just be able to reinstall MSstatsPTM as it's dependencies include the other packages.

Let me know if you have any more questions!

Best,

Devon

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Add site into ProteinName column
raw_ptm_df$ProteinName <- paste(raw_ptm_df$ProteinName, raw_ptm_df$Site, sep = "_")

# Run MSstatsTMT Converters
PTM.data <- MSstatsTMT::PDtoMSstatsTMTFormat(raw_ptm_df, annotation)
PROTEIN.data <- MSstatsTMT::PDtoMSstatsTMTFormat(raw_protein_df,annotation) # If Protein data not available just skip this part

# Combine into one list
raw.input <- list(PTM = PTM.data,
                  PROTEIN = PROTEIN.data) # Use PROTEIN = NULL if protein data not available

groupComparisonPlots(data=test.pairwise$ComparisonResult,

On Thursday, July 8, 2021 at 7:53:16 AM UTC-5 devonj...@gmail.com wrote:
> Hi Mi,
>
> Hopefully I can clear up a couple of your questions! In terms of going from PD to MSstatsPTM, we do not have a direct converter right now. I have included a brief piece of code that uses the MSstatsTMT converter to put the raw data into MSstatsPTM format. If you have an example phospho PD dataset you can share, I would be happy to work on building a converter directly into MSstatsPTM.
>
> 1. The "PTM" and "Protein" datasets should really be two separate MS runs, one phosphorylated and the other not. The non-phosphorylated run is used to adjusted the modified peptides for changes in protein abundance. If you do not have a unmodified MS run, the package can still be run with the "PTM" data only, you just will not be able to do a protein level adjustment..
>
> 2. MSstatsPTM is the correct package and can handle TMT experiments now.
>
> 3. The versioning is a little different due to Bioconductor's latest release. All packages in Bioconductor v3.12 (the newest version) require R v4.1. I would recommend upgrading your R to version v4.1 and then upgrading the MSstats packages. You should just be able to reinstall MSstatsPTM as it's dependencies include the other packages.
>
> Let me know if you have any more questions!
>
> Best,
>
> Devon
>
> ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
> # Add site into ProteinName column
> raw_ptm_df$ProteinName <- paste(raw_ptm_df$ProteinName, raw_ptm_df$Site, sep = "_")
>
> # Run MSstatsTMT Converters
> PTM.data <- MSstatsTMT::PDtoMSstatsTMTFormat(raw_ptm_df, annotation)
> PROTEIN.data <- MSstatsTMT::PDtoMSstatsTMTFormat(raw_protein_df,annotation) # If Protein data not available just skip this part
>
> # Combine into one list
> raw.input <- list(PTM = PTM.data,
>                   PROTEIN = PROTEIN.data) # Use PROTEIN = NULL if protein data not available
>

You can use parameters sig (FDR cutoff for the adjusted p-values) and FCcutoff (fold change cutoff) to change the definition of red color in the volcano plot.

The following code can generate a wide table with channels in the column:

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
data <- proteinSummarization$ProteinLevelData
data_wide <- data %>%
  mutate(ID = paste(Run, Channel, sep = "-")) %>%
  select(Protein, ID, Abundance) %>%
  spread(ID, Abundance)
head(data_wide)

-Ting

messages.subject: MSstatsTMT and Batch Effects
messages.body_plain:
Hi Support Team,

I'm currently running an analysis in MSstatsTMT on a dataset that has batch effects. It’s a TMTpro dataset with four treatment groups and four replicates where the replicates were prepared in batches (i.e. the 4 samples for replicate 1 on day 1, 4 samples for replicate 2 on day 2, etc). We see batch effects between samples prepared on different days. Is there a way to specify this sort of batch effect in the annotation file? I have tried running the data through MSstats as technical or biological replicates but it's hard to tell if the effects have been corrected for. I have been evaluating this by creating a PCA plot (attached) after the proteinSummarization step or by generating ProfilePlots but I suspect batch effects might be taken into consideration in the groupComparison step.

I was wondering, does MSstats compensate for batch effects? If it does but in the groupComparison step, how would you recommend evaluating this?

Thanks,

Emily

messages.subject: MSstats of MSE acquisition method optimizations
messages.subject_clean: MSstats of MSE acquisition method optimizations
messages.body_plain:
Part 1

Dear MSstats team,

First of all thanks for the awesome lectures on the May Institute 2021 meeting. The material has been really instructive and helpful. Also, thank you Prof. Vitek for the input she has already provided!

Now, this might be an abnormally long post so I please ask for some patiences with me.

We have been testing multiple mass spectrometry acquisition approaches in our Synapt G2-Si using TWIMS with the aim to improve sensitivity of fragment ions. We wished to evaluate differences introduced only by the different acquisition methods used with respect to peptide identification and quantitative signal detected (AUC of EIC chromatograms with background area subtraction in the case of Skylile) so we analyzed the same sample over and over from same vial injection with LC-MS/MS with MSE (a type of DIA) acquisition approaches.

After data curation and MStats implementation on Skyline we have come up with some very promising results for the aimed goal: improve MS2 sensitivity. Differences at the MS1 level are due to instrumental limitations for the scanning range that affects the effective duty cyle of the TOF (i.e. effectiveness of sampling the ion beam) for the respective experiment setup. The results look as expected: 1) a systematic increase for (almost) all peptide fragment ion signal for seMSE vs the others and 2) the changes with respect to precursor ions are less drastic and up to some point signal is decreased due to the limitation of having to use a less efficient TOF duty cycle for precursor ion detection in the seMSE method.

Using MSstats Skyline external tool and R-ggplot of the results we generated the following (attached) figure: EColi_MPDS - Volcano (peptides) - DIA comparisons.png

My concerns are with respect to the accuracy of estimated fold changes and the significance of this. Let's take as an example peptide K.YIAETFLEDAR.E [27, 37] (P0ABP8) with some EICs for the seMSE (left) vs MSE (right).

See Skyline snippet attached figure: Peptide example.png

As you can see in the MSE (right) example, EICs generated for some of the fragments is very poor and one could argue that is just integrated noise signal (e.g. y7 EIC). If it is indeed noise, then I wouldn't expect the variation to be remotely similar between the two cases. From my beginners and dusty stats knowledge, I remember that similar variability of compared data sets is a required parameter for a correct t-test comparison. How would this affect the validity of the reported t-test?

Prof. Vitek comment on this concern:

"I agree that the bottom-right EIC looks like noise, and it may be better to treat them as “analyze below the limit of quantification” rather than integrating the noise and providing specific quantitative values. If your dataset has many features in this situation, it may be the reason why the volcano plot for MS2 looks strange...the command-line MSstats views peptides such as in the bottom-right corner as censored, and does not use their values...it may be best to switch to the most recent version available through the command line."

So I went ahead and tried to process the results in R-Studio and I am attaching the generated Profile Plots, the input, and short R-script used to process the data (MSstats_ouput <https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1IQjGhvdR5hXn9CUXC_wqrhBskfDpYca7?usp=sharing>). The R-script was written based on Meena's excellent live demonstration, but I am not sure what I am doing wrong because every time I try to use the groupComparisons() function RStudio goes completely bonkers and unresponsive until I have to force quit it with the task manager. It doesn't seem to be "overloading" the PC (attached screenshot: RStudio_error.png); Processor: Intel(R) Xeon(R) CPU E5-2650 v3 @ 2.30 GHz 2.30 GHz; RAM: 16 GB

Questions:

Besides the figuring out what is going on with the error I also have a few questions:

When exportin the "MSstats-input.csv" report from Skyline it is ignoring transitions marked as "Non-quantitative"? Or treating them as censored?

Would it be valid to report the summarized results with the above Volcano plots? Or should I consider other sort of presentation of the data since when you see a volcano plot in the proteomics community we expect most things don't change and only a few stand out, while here, based on the experimental design, a systematic change of all signals is expected.

Due to the systematic change of fragment ion signal between MS methods I don't think I can rely on "borrowing the variance from other measurements" so I have opted for not using any sort of sinal normalization. Is this correct to do?

On the ProfilePot_wSummarization the Processed feature-level data and Ru_summary (protein level?) trends look very distinct for seMSE and UDMSE, why is that?

In Skyline I marked each of the replicates with each MS method as "BioReplicates" but on a more routine condition comparison experiment this would technically be technical replicates? How should these be treated and what complications could this have with statistical testing?

If you made it this far on the thread I sincerely thank you for your time and hope to hear back from you. I know it is a lot and if it makes it easier I would be happy to accomodate my schedule for a zoom meeting to illustrate the data and discuss.

Sincerely,

Juan C.

messages.subject: Re: MSstats of MSE acquisition method optimizations
messages.subject_clean: MSstats of MSE acquisition method optimizations
messages.body_plain:
Hi Juan,

Thanks much for the detailed documentation of the questions.

I will let the team to answer the implementation questions, but will try to answer the statistical ones.

Q: Would it be valid to report the summarized results with the above Volcano plots? Or should I consider other sort of presentation of the data since when you see a volcano plot in the proteomics community we expect most things don't change and only a few stand out, while here, based on the experimental design, a systematic change of all signals is expected.
If I understand the experiment correctly, the overall approach in MSstats is not applicable to your experimental design.

Statistical analyses such as in MSstats (but also others, such as in Limma etc) assume that we are interested in a population-level quantity (difference in average protein abundance between two populations with two conditions), with the understanding that the measurements are comparable between the conditions.

Yes your case is the opposite. You only have one population quantity (the sample is unchanged), but two different measurement strategies that are not directly comparable. So the null hypothesis that you test in fact does not make sense.

A better approach is to consider each acquisition separately. Normalize the runs (e.g., by equalizing medians) separately for each acquisition. Then consider profile plots (of fragment ions, precursor ions, or their protein-level summaries) and compare the summaries such as the mean, the standard deviation, and the cv. Noisy fragments such as in your plot will manifest themselves by smaller means, higher standard deviations and cvs. This will be a sufficient criterion for a comparison.

Q: Due to the systematic change of fragment ion signal between MS methods I don't think I can rely on "borrowing the variance from other measurements" so I have opted for not using any sort of sinal normalization. Is this correct to do?
Yeah, the whole approach is not meaningful, and this includes the normalization.

Q: On the ProfilePot_wSummarization the Processed feature-level data and Ru_summary (protein level?) trends look very distinct for seMSE and UDMSE, why is that?
Probably due to other methodological issues. See if the problem persists after the two separate analyses suggested above.

Q: In Skyline I marked each of the replicates with each MS method as "BioReplicates" but on a more routine condition comparison experiment this would technically be technical replicates? How should these be treated and what complications could this have with statistical testing?
They should be viewed as technical replicates, since you only have one biological sample. It is enough for making the profile plots suggested above.

Hope that this helps at least somewhat!

Sincerely
Olga

messages.body_plain:
Hi,
as for the "Non-quantitative" transitions, currently, they are not treated separately in Skyline converter. If the corresponding intensity values are 0, they will be treated as censored. Otherwise, missing at random (if NA), or as regular intensities. You can treat them separately before passing data to the converter function. We might add a processing step for such intensities in a future release. I'll look at these intensities while checking the groupComparison problem.
KInd regards,
Mateusz

messages.subject: Re: MSstatsTMT and Batch Effects
messages.body_plain:
Hi Emily,

Since global normalization is already applied, another local normalization for each protein separately seems required to remove the batch effects between days. Unfortunately, MSstats only provides such an option to remove batch effects between mixtures using reference channels, not within the mixture.

My recommendation is
(1) Use Day information as BioReplicate in the annotation file.
(2) Treat Day as Mixture. Then groupComparisonTMT() will take into the Mixture (Day) effect in the statistical modeling.

global.raw <- MaxQtoMSstatsTMTFormat(evidence = evidence,
                                     proteinGroups = proteinGroups,

                                     annotation = annotation, # BioReplicate column stores the day information

                                     useUniquePeptide = FALSE)

global.quant <- proteinSummarization(global.raw,
                                     global_norm = TRUE,
                                     reference_norm = FALSE)

# Use day as Mixture
temp <- global.quant$ProteinLevelData
temp$Mixture <- temp$BioReplicate. # BioReplicate stores the day information
global.quant[["ProteinLevelData"]] <- temp

global.comp <- groupComparisonTMT(global.quant,
                                  moderated = TRUE,
                                  save_fitted_models = TRUE)

Best,
Ting
